incident-bot: page fired — GPU memory pressure on pool=decoder-eu-west node=gpu-24 error=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY; alarm_id=oom_spike_321; runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory-oom
PagerDuty: Incident P123456 auto-triggered (severity: P2). Assigned to rotation: @oncall_beth. Escalation policy: 8m -> senior-sre.
oncall_beth: I'm taking this. seeing repeated CUDA_ALLOC_FAILED in logs and NVML reports GPU memory at ~98% on gpu-24. Affected model: text-generation-v2.
jordan: any customer-facing errors yet? request rate?
oncall_beth: 503s observed from the frontend where requests hit decoder-eu-west. 3 unique downstream services reporting failures. 503 spike started ~2m ago. I'm going to cordon & drain the node, then restart the runtime.
infra_rohit: recommended steps to evacuate:```bash
kubectl cordon node/gpu-24
kubectl drain node/gpu-24 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
# scale up pool to absorb traffic
kubectl scale deployment/decoder-eu-west --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy decoder-eu-west -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2))
```
oncall_beth: running drain now. starting eviction of long-lived KV caches for text-generation-v2 sessions. enabling kvcache aggressive-evict for this pool.
incident-bot: auto-evacuation in progress. rerouting ~35% of new traffic to fallback-model small-gen-x to reduce memory pressure.
customer_success_maya: FYI we have one paying customer (AcmeCorp) reporting increased timeouts. CS oncall notified them and gave a heads-up that engineering is investigating.
jordan: if drain/restart doesn't help, consider fallback to quantized-model or roll driver back; any recent infra changes?
oncall_beth: no config changes in last 24h. there was a model rollout 6h ago but only traffic-light staged. suspecting KV cache growth from long conversational sessions.
oncall_beth: restarted inference container on gpu-24 and forced GC on KV. freed ~12GiB according to nvidia-smi. NVML now shows GPU memory at 12%. errors dropped immediately.
sre_lead_claire: nice. keep node cordoned for 30m and monitor for recurrence. please collect kernel & driver logs and upload to the incident bundle.
oncall_beth: logs collected: /mnt/scratch/incidents/4823456789/gpu-24-logs.tar.gz. captured: dmesg, journalctl, nvidia-smi -q, container logs. I created follow-up Jira: INF-7892 (suspected kvcache leak).
PagerDuty: Incident P123456 acknowledged by @oncall_beth. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.
customer_success_maya: AcmeCorp updated: brief outage ~4 minutes, errors resolved. they asked for postmortem; offering to review with them tomorrow.
jordan: please add an alert refinement: fire when nvml memory > 90% for >2m (we currently alert at 95%), and add kvcache eviction metric.
oncall_beth: noted. immediate remediation applied: aggressive kvcache eviction for decoder-eu-west, cordoned node, restarted runtime, scaled pool +2. action items: 1) postmortem + logs (INF-7892), 2) add eviction and mem>90% alerts, 3) test auto-reclaim policy.
sre_lead_claire: leaving this in monitoring. if it reappears escalate to senior-sre per policy. good work team :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident P123456 closed for mitigated state; follow-up assigned INF-7892. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-memory-oom. Timeline: page -> 0m, drain start -> +2m, restart -> +6m, errors resolved -> +10m.
